pairs.subject: conformance-checking
pairs.evidence: lib/testing/gateLadder.test.ts:83 The gate-ladder conformance check (CI must be a superset of `npm run check`) matches substrings, not tokens. `npm run check` chains both `test` and `test:rules`, and both `docs:sync` and `docs:sync:test`, so deleting `npm run test` (ci.yml:49) or `npm run docs:sync` (ci.yml:75) from CI still passes because `npm run test:rules` / `npm run docs:sync:test` contain the shorter string. That is a false pass, and no fixture exists that would have caught it.

techniques.evidence: lib/testing/gateLadder.test.ts:83 Substring where token was meant: 'npm run test' is satisfied by 'npm run test:rules', and 'npm run docs:sync' by 'npm run docs:sync:test'. Line 96 has the same defect (cmd.includes(k) for CI_ONLY_BY_DESIGN keys such as 'build').

lib/testing/gateLadder.test.ts:39 The checker only ever reads the live package.json and ci.yml. No fixture workflow that drops a step proves it can go red, which is exactly what would have exposed the substring false pass.
lib/testing/contextMapRefs.test.ts:60 The derived ref walk asserts a population floor (700) before asserting zero dangling refs. gateLadder.test.ts:78 and revalidateParity.test.ts:100 do the same.

lib/testing/gateLadder.test.ts:48 Accepted asymmetries are named one per step, each with its cost-reason, and lines 104-109 check that every entry still exists. Partial: entries carry no date or standard version.
lib/testing/contextMapRefs.test.ts:67 No percentage is emitted. The failure count carries its denominator, so the number carries its predicate.

pairs.subject: conformance-checking
pairs.evidence: lib/testing/sentinel/invariants.ts:405 The sentinel is a registry of 18 independent invariants, but its fixtures are hand-written test cases rather than enumerated from this roster. As a result, law-provenance-uniformity, graph-provenance-uniformity, amends-closure and loader-degradations appear in tests only as "ok" (sentinel.test.ts:270-273) and are never shown to fire, and adding a new invariant with no red fixture fails nothing.

techniques.evidence: lib/testing/sentinel/invariants.ts:405 The roster is enumerated only for labels and order (sentinel.test.ts:678). No harness requires each id to have a fail fixture, and 4 of the 18 have none anywhere in the test tree (grep of **/*.test.ts). The flake register does it right: one refusing case per rule in registry.test.ts:75.

lib/testing/sentinel/sentinel.test.ts:120 Covers the fresh-install shape (empty store), the conformant shape (clean store, line 142, asserting the exact check id/status list) and targeted non-conformant stores, all asserting structured ids rather than prose.

lib/testing/sentinel/report.ts:201 Unable-to-check ('unevaluable') is a separate status from pass and violation and is counted in the headline summary. No warning rung exists, which is acceptable under 'do not add rungs for taste'.

lib/testing/sentinel/sentinel.test.ts:138 A false pass was hunted down and fixed: an empty audit ledger used to read as 'trivially valid' ok (comment at line 137, until 2026-08-13) and now reads as unevaluable.

lib/testing/flake/registry.ts:40 Accepted test failures (quarantine) are a dated register: each entry has owner, entered date, expiry, cause and evidence. Expired entries turn the gate red (registry.test.ts:55), and a 60-day maximum span is enforced.

lib/testing/flake/detect.ts:55 Refuses to emit a transition rate below 4 comparable same-HEAD runs. Figures name their window, HEAD and run count, and the sentinel uses counts with denominators, never a rate (sentinel.test.ts:276).

pairs.subject: conformance-checking
pairs.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:60 The harness enumerates the rule set from the filesystem (rules/, docs/rules/, __tests__/) and from the plugin export, and requires all four to equal one list. A rule added without a RuleTester suite or a doc page fails discovery, and every suite carries invalid cases asserting messageIds.

techniques.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:60 The rule set is cross-checked across exports, rule files, docs and suites (lines 57-60), so no hand allow-map can hide a rule. All 10 suites have both valid and invalid arrays.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:58 The filesystem-derived listing is compared against a committed list rather than only against another derivation, so an empty listing goes red instead of passing silently.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/no-silent-catch.test.mjs:57 Each rule is proven red by its invalid fixtures, and assertions target structured finding ids (messageId), not rendered text.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/no-silent-catch.test.mjs:49 Valid cases pin the false-fail shapes (catchAll as a substring, computed ["catch"]), so narrowing or widening the detector trips the suite.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:116 When the shim check cannot run it reports SKIP rather than PASS, and only MODULE_NOT_FOUND is downgraded (other errors rethrow). Preset severities are also pinned per rule at lines 93-102.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:122 No percentage is computed. The harness prints a suite count with its predicate only.

declined.subject: conformance-checking
declined.reason: withdrawn after review: reviewer (sonnet): The anchor lib/claims/registry.ts:115 is the ISSUED_FIGURES declaration, which does not show that a conformance checker is absent. The not-applicable rests only on a grep for conformance, conformant and waiver, and those may not be the right terms for a registry that re-derives and gates claim refs.
